examples.solution_text:
The curve lies to the right of the $y$-axis throughout the interval.
$\begin{align*} A&=\int_1^2 2y^2\,dy\\&=\left[\frac{2y^3}{3}\right]_1^2\\&=\frac{16}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\\&=\frac{14}{3}\ \text{units}^2\end{align*}$

The curve lies to the left of the $y$-axis, so take the negative of the integral.
$\begin{align*} A&=-\int_1^3(-y^2)\,dy\\&=-\left[-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_1^3\\&=-\left(-9+\frac{1}{3}\right)\\&=\frac{26}{3}\ \text{units}^2\end{align*}$

Make $x$ the subject.
$\begin{align*} y^2&=3x+1\\x&=\frac{y^2-1}{3}\end{align*}$
Here $x\geq0$ for $1\leq y\leq4$.
$\begin{align*} A&=\int_1^4\frac{y^2-1}{3}\,dy\\&=\left[\frac{y^3}{9}-\frac{y}{3}\right]_1^4\\&=\left(\frac{64}{9}-\frac{4}{3}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{3}\right)\\&=6\ \text{units}^2\end{align*}$

methods.description: For a region wholly left of the y-axis, negate the definite integral to obtain positive area.

methods.description: Make x the subject, retain the supplied y limits and integrate with respect to y.

examples.derivation: For 1≤y≤2, x=2y² is positive. Its primitive is 2y³/3, giving area 16/3−2/3=14/3 square units. The diagram shades precisely the region between this curve and x=0 over these bounds.
For 1≤y≤3, x=−y² is negative. The signed integral is [−y³/3]₁³=−26/3; negating gives 26/3 square units. The diagram places the specified region left of the y-axis.

Rearranging gives x=(y²−1)/3, nonnegative on [1,4]. The primitive y³/9−y/3 has values 52/9 and −2/9 at the endpoints, giving area 6 square units. The diagram uses the correct nonnegative-y branch and boundaries.

The x endpoints 0 and 3 give y endpoints 2 and 29. Rearranging gives x=(y−2)^(1/3). Integrating yields [3(y−2)^(4/3)/4]₂²⁹=243/4 square units. Both diagrams show the correct region; converted bounds and the point (3,29) are annotated only in the solution.

Zeros occur at y=0 and 4. The curve is left of the axis on (0,4) and right on (4,6]. With G(y)=y³/3−2y², G(0)=0, G(4)=−32/3 and G(6)=0. The two positive areas are each 32/3, totalling 64/3 square units. The diagrams match both regions, with the split annotation confined to the solution.
